chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man has estates, some of them near each other. He goes out and stays in them. Should he pray complete or shorten?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Complete'.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: To shorten the prayer (to two rak'ahs)

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler with nearby estates pray complete or short prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the boundary of travel (*safar*) by establishing that proximity of one's own properties negates the status of a traveler, thereby requiring full prayer (*salat al-tamam*). It reflects the Shia juristic principle that owning multiple estates in close vicinity does not extend the travel period, distinguishing it from cases where properties are distant. This ruling underscores the practical application of *qasr* (shortening prayers) based on physical distance rather than mere ownership of multiple locations.
